assignments.why: A tool-use task-automation benchmark (agent evaluation benchmarks) whose requests are generated by sampling tool subgraphs and back-instructing an LLM (self-evolving tests).
Automatically constructs fresh test sets from post-cutoff texts to avoid contamination (generated test sets).
Trains a process reward model from Monte Carlo step labels and uses it for reranking and PPO.
LLMs act as qualified reviewer-judges (LLM judges) in a peer-review scheme (alternative paradigm) whose weighted reviews are aggregated into a ranking (social choice).

assignments.note: 2024-01 Scalable meta-evaluation via agent debate ScaleEval
assignments.why: Meta-evaluates LLM evaluators (audits) using multi-agent debate (alternative paradigm) and escalates to humans only when agents disagree (escalation).
Trains a model as its own judge (trained judges), via DPO on self-judged preference pairs (preference learning), with the judge improving across iterations (self-improving judge).
Live-web multimodal agent benchmark (agent benchmarks) scored by GPT-4V judging trajectory screenshots, with judge-human agreement reported (LLM judges).
Multi-agent framework that reframes benchmark instances into new evolving test instances.
A benchmark measuring LLMs' critique and correction ability (meta-evaluation of judges), whose subject is the act of critiquing (LLM judges).
RL red teaming with novelty rewards to generate diverse adversarial test prompts.

assignments.note: 2024-02 Debating with more persuasive LLMs leads to more truthful answers
assignments.why: Studies debate versus consultancy as an evaluation protocol (alternative paradigm) and measures how non-expert LLM and human judges' accuracy depends on it (judging).
Probing agents transform benchmark questions into fresh generated variants.

assignments.note: 2024-02 Humans or LLMs as the Judge
assignments.why: Empirical study of misinformation, gender, authority and beauty biases in human and LLM judges, and their use to attack judges.
Measures judge robustness to universal adversarial phrases and compares absolute versus comparative scoring.

Interactive multi-turn examination instead of static scoring (alternative paradigm), dynamically generated contamination-resistant questions (self-evolving tests), scored by an evaluator LLM (LLM judges).
Trains a two-head RLHF reward model separating length from quality (reward model training on preference data).
Unsupervised peer review among models (alternative paradigm) that aggregates their mutual scores with optimised capability weights (social choice), models acting as judges (LLM judges).
Quality-diversity search that grows an archive of generated adversarial prompts against a target.
Uses the model's self-evaluation as the judge (LLM judges) to build DPO preference pairs (preference learning), with a tuning step that improves the self-evaluator's calibration (calibration).
LLM-generated unit tests (generated test sets) filtered by build, pass and coverage execution checks (execution-based verification).
An examiner LLM generates the next questions from how models answered (adaptive generated tests) and judges the answers (LLM judge).

assignments.note: 2024-02 Unsupervised evaluation of code LLMs with round-trip correctness
assignments.why: Label-free evaluation by round-trip consistency checked with execution tests.

Prediction-powered inference combines many judge labels with a small human set for sample-size reduction with valid error control (stopping rules), making judge-based evaluation unbiased (LLM judges).
Crowdsourced pairwise arena (alternative paradigm) ranked with Bradley-Terry (preference learning) by aggregating many voters' judgments into a leaderboard (social choice).
A judge design replacing Likert scores with decomposed binary checklist questions to make LLM judging more reliable.
Evolves HumanEval problems into new LLM-generated variants.

assignments.note: 2024-03 Fine-tuned Judge is not a General Substitute for GPT-4
assignments.why: Empirical study (audit) of fine-tuned judges JudgeLM, PandaLM, Auto-J and Prometheus (trained judges) on generalisability and fairness.
Optimised prompt-injection attacks on LLM judges and evaluation of defences (adversarial cues, robustness).
Continuously refreshed, time-windowed contamination-free test set of new contest problems.
A meta-evaluation benchmark (audits) of reward models (trained judges) built from chosen/rejected preference pairs (preference learning).
